ui.occurrence.step.UpdateStorageDriver: Look for an update to the disk controller driver (SATA or NVMe) on the website of your PC or motherboard maker.
ui.occurrence.step.CheckDiskCable: On a desktop PC, swap the disk's cable or the port it uses on the motherboard.
ui.occurrence.step.RunDiskTest: Read the whole disk in Tests: it finds the parts that do not read.
ui.occurrence.step.FindDiskHeavyApp: If it happens again, open Now to see who is using the disk, and pause what can wait.
ui.occurrence.step.CloseMemoryHeavyApp: Close the programs and tabs you are not using, to free memory.
ui.occurrence.step.CheckCooling: Check that the air vents are clear and the fan spins; clean out the dust.
ui.occurrence.step.CheckPowerPlan: On a laptop, plug it in and pick the best performance power mode.
ui.occurrence.step.UpdateGpuDriver: Update the graphics driver from its maker's website or app.
ui.occurrence.step.EnableSensitiveMode: If it freezes again, turn on sensitive mode from the tray: for 30 minutes Vestigium watches more closely.
ui.occurrence.step.ReportToAppVendor: If it happens again, update or reinstall {app}; if it keeps happening, tell its makers.

ui.occurrence.step.UpdateDriver: Update the driver {driver} from its maker's website or Windows Update.
ui.occurrence.step.UpdateDriver.any: Update the graphics and chipset drivers from the website of your PC or motherboard maker, or through Windows Update.
ui.occurrence.step.BackUpNow: Copy the files that matter from {disk} to another disk or to the cloud today.

ui.occurrence.step.LetWindowsManagePageF: In System Properties › Advanced › Performance › Virtual memory, let Windows manage the page file size.
ui.occurrence.step.CheckHardwareStabilit: If the processor, memory or graphics card is overclocked, go back to the factory values; then check that the PC is not overheating.
ui.occurrence.step.KeepOneAntivirus: Keep one antivirus on: uninstall the other, or turn off its real-time protection.
ui.occurrence.step.ReviewStartupApps: Review the apps that open with Windows (Task Manager › Startup apps) and turn off the ones you do not need right away.
ui.occurrence.step.WaitForShutdown: Wait for the screen and the PC's lights to go off before cutting the power at the socket or power strip.
ui.occurrence.step.MoveWindowsToSsd: If you can, move Windows to an SSD: it is the upgrade that helps the most.

ui.health.kind.DiskSmart.why.Critical: The disk itself worked out that it is going to fail. Your files still open, but that can change from one day to the next.
ui.health.kind.DiskSmart.why.Attention: The disk swapped damaged areas for spares or reported errors it could not fix. A few happen; a number that keeps growing means wear.
ui.health.kind.DiskSmart.rule: Critical with PredictFailure, an NVMe critical warning or spare below its threshold. Attention with SMART 5, 187, 188, 197 or 198 above 0, NVMe use at 90% or more, or NVMe media errors.
ui.health.kind.StorageErrors.title.Criti: A disk reported areas it could not read
ui.health.kind.StorageErrors.title.Atten: Windows had to reset or retry a disk
ui.health.kind.StorageErrors.tech: Disk errors in the System log, 30 days
ui.health.kind.StorageErrors.why.Critica: Windows logged areas of a disk it could not read. Files kept there may already be damaged.
ui.health.kind.StorageErrors.why.Attenti: Windows lost contact with a disk for a moment and had to reset the connection or repeat what it asked. Often a driver or a cable.
ui.health.kind.StorageErrors.rule: Critical with a bad-block or paging error in 30 days. Attention with a storage reset or a retried disk operation in 30 days.
ui.health.kind.LowSpace.title: Little free space on the Windows disk ({subject})
ui.health.kind.LowSpace.why: With less than 10% free, Windows has little room for updates and for the page file to grow when memory runs short.
ui.health.kind.LowSpace.rule: Attention below 10% free; critical below 5% or 5 GB. Closes above 12%.
ui.health.kind.WindowsOnHdd.title: Windows is on a hard disk
ui.health.kind.WindowsOnHdd.why: A hard disk (HDD) is much slower than an SSD when many programs read at once, and Windows does that all the time.
ui.health.kind.WindowsOnHdd.rule: Attention when the disk that holds the Windows folder has a seek penalty (HDD).
ui.health.kind.DirtyRestarts.title.Criti: The PC went down with a blue screen
ui.health.kind.DirtyRestarts.title.Atten: The PC restarted without shutting down
ui.health.kind.DirtyRestarts.why.Critica: Windows stopped with a blue screen this week. One can be chance; more point to a driver, the memory or overheating.
ui.health.kind.DirtyRestarts.why.Attenti: The PC lost power or stopped while in use more than once this month: a power cut, the power button held down, or a hang that let nothing be written.
ui.health.kind.DirtyRestarts.rule: Attention with 2 or more Kernel-Power 41 outside shutdown in 30 days; critical with a bug check in 7 days.
ui.health.kind.ShutdownUnfinished.title: Shutdown does not reach the end
ui.health.kind.ShutdownUnfinished.why: The PC lost power while it was still shutting down. Maybe the power is cut before the screen goes dark, or something holds the shutdown up. It is not a fall while you use the PC.
ui.health.kind.ShutdownUnfinished.rule: Attention with 2 or more Kernel-Power 41 whose SleepInProgress is 6 (shutting down) in 30 days.
ui.health.kind.FailuresRising.title: More failures than usual this week
ui.health.kind.FailuresRising.tech: Failures in 7 days against the weekly average of the 4 weeks before
ui.health.kind.FailuresRising.why: Windows logged at least twice as many failures this week (programs that crashed, falls, hangs, errors) as in an average week before.
ui.health.kind.FailuresRising.rule: Attention with 3 or more failures in 7 days and at least twice the weekly average of the 4 weeks before.
ui.health.kind.NoCrashDump.title: A blue screen would leave no record
ui.health.kind.NoCrashDump.why: Windows could not prepare the file where it writes what happened in a blue screen, usually because the page file is off or too small. If the PC falls, there will be nothing to read afterwards.
ui.health.kind.NoCrashDump.rule: Attention with volmgr 46 (crash dump initialization failed) in 30 days.
ui.health.kind.MemoryOften.title: Memory runs short often
ui.health.kind.MemoryOften.tech: Memory in use above 85%, days of the last 7
ui.health.kind.MemoryOften.why: On several days this week, memory in use went above 85%. Then Windows uses the disk in its place and everything slows down.
ui.health.kind.MemoryOften.rule: Attention with 3 of the last 7 days above 85% memory in use; closes at 1 day or fewer.
ui.health.kind.PageFile.tech: Page file and commit charge, 7 days
ui.health.kind.PageFile.why.Critical: This week, memory in use came close to the limit Windows can promise programs (memory plus the page file). Past it, programs fail or close.
ui.health.kind.PageFile.why.Attention: Without a page file, memory has no room to stretch, and a blue screen leaves no record.
ui.health.kind.PageFile.rule: Critical with a commit peak of 90% of the limit or more in 7 days, or Resource-Exhaustion 2004; attention with no page file. Closes below 80%.
ui.health.kind.SlowBoot.title: Startup takes long
ui.health.kind.SlowBoot.why: Windows measured how long the PC takes to start, and some steps took longer than they should.
ui.health.kind.SlowBoot.rule: Attention when the last startup took more than 90 s or Windows flagged a slow step in 30 days; healthy up to 60 s.
ui.health.kind.HardwareErrors.title.Crit: The hardware reported a fatal error
ui.health.kind.HardwareErrors.why: The processor, the memory or a slot reported an error to Windows. Corrected ones can come before failures; a fatal one takes the PC down.
ui.health.kind.HardwareErrors.rule: Attention with any WHEA-Logger error in 30 days; critical when one is fatal (WHEA-Logger 18).
ui.health.kind.DisplayResets.title: The graphics driver keeps restarting
ui.health.kind.DisplayResets.why: When the graphics card stops answering, Windows restarts its driver: the screen blinks or freezes for a moment. Twice or more in a week is worth acting on.
ui.health.kind.DisplayResets.rule: Attention with 2 or more Display 4101 in 7 days; critical with 5 or more.
ui.health.kind.Throttling.title: The processor was held back
ui.health.kind.Throttling.why: The firmware limited the processor's speed, usually because of heat or the power plan. Everything runs slower while it lasts.
ui.health.kind.Throttling.rule: Attention with any Kernel-Processor-Power 37 in 7 days.
ui.health.kind.TwoAntivirus.title: Two antivirus programs are on
ui.health.kind.TwoAntivirus.tech: Windows Security Center: real-time products on
ui.health.kind.TwoAntivirus.why: Two antivirus programs scanning in real time get in each other's way and slow the PC down without making it safer.
ui.health.kind.TwoAntivirus.rule: Attention with 2 or more antivirus products on in Windows Security Center.

ui.tweaks.what.FastStartup: When you shut down, Windows hibernates its core to start faster. Sometimes that shutdown never finishes.
ui.tweaks.what.FastStartup.tech: Fast Startup: at shutdown the kernel and drivers go to hiberfil.sys (hybrid boot).
ui.tweaks.what.Hibernation: Keeps the memory in a file so the PC can hibernate; the file is as large as a good part of the memory.
ui.tweaks.what.Hibernation.tech: hiberfil.sys on the system drive; turned off through SystemReserveHiberFile.
ui.tweaks.what.PowerPlan: Power saver slows the processor down to save energy, which a desktop on mains power does not need.
ui.tweaks.what.PowerPlan.tech: Active scheme Power saver to Balanced, through PowerSetActiveScheme.
ui.tweaks.what.PcieAspm: Switches the link to the disk and the network off for moments to save energy. On some boards it causes stutters.
ui.tweaks.what.PcieAspm.tech: Link State Power Management of the active scheme, plugged-in value.
ui.tweaks.what.UsbSuspend: Turns idle USB ports off to save energy. Sometimes a device is slow to come back.
ui.tweaks.what.UsbSuspend.tech: USB selective suspend of the active scheme, plugged-in value.
ui.tweaks.what.SysMain: Loads the programs you use most into memory ahead of time. On a hard disk, that keeps the disk busy.
ui.tweaks.what.SysMain.tech: SysMain: prefetching and memory compression; on a hard disk it reads the system disk at random.
ui.tweaks.what.WindowsSearch: Reads your files so Windows search finds them fast.
ui.tweaks.what.WindowsSearch.tech: WSearch service with SearchIndexer.exe and its helpers.
ui.tweaks.what.GameDvr: Keeps recording the last minutes of a game so you can save a moment afterwards. It weighs on the video and the disk.
ui.tweaks.what.GameDvr.tech: Xbox Game Bar background capture: constant video encoding while a game runs.
ui.tweaks.what.GpuScheduling: Lets the video card organise its own work. On some PCs it helps, on others it causes stutters.
ui.tweaks.what.GpuScheduling.tech: Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling, HwSchMode 2 on and 1 off.
ui.tweaks.what.Mpo: A Windows shortcut for drawing video and games. With two monitors it sometimes flickers or stutters.
ui.tweaks.what.Mpo.tech: Multiplane overlay, turned off by OverlayTestMode = 5.
ui.tweaks.what.StartupApp: Opens by itself when you sign in to Windows.
ui.tweaks.what.StartupApp.tech: Run entry turned off through Explorer's StartupApproved, as Task Manager does.
ui.tweaks.what.AppDumps: When an app closes by itself, Windows keeps what happened in a small file the Dumps page reads.
ui.tweaks.what.AppDumps.tech: Creates the WER LocalDumps key with DumpType 1 (minidump) and DumpCount 10.
ui.tweaks.what.CrashDump: Decides what Windows writes when the PC falls with a blue screen.
ui.tweaks.risk.FastStartup: The PC starts a few seconds slower.
ui.tweaks.risk.Hibernation: Fast startup and the option to hibernate go with it.
ui.tweaks.risk.PowerPlan: The PC uses a little more energy.
ui.tweaks.risk.PcieAspm: Plugged in, the PC uses a little more energy.
ui.tweaks.risk.UsbSuspend: Plugged in, the PC uses a little more energy.
ui.tweaks.risk.SysMain: Programs you use all the time may open a little slower.
ui.tweaks.risk.GameDvr: The shortcut to save what just happened stops working.
ui.tweaks.risk.GpuScheduling: Some games run better with it on; you can switch back.
ui.tweaks.risk.Mpo: Usually changes nothing outside flicker cases.
ui.tweaks.risk.StartupApp: Nothing is deleted: open the app when you need it, or turn it back on here.
ui.tweaks.risk.AppDumps: Each dump takes a few MB.
ui.tweaks.risk.CrashDump: A complete dump can take as much disk space as the memory.
ui.tweaks.why_not.FastStartup: No fall while shutting down in 30 days, and no open Health point about it.
ui.tweaks.why_not.Hibernation: The system drive is not short of space.
ui.tweaks.why_not.PowerPlan: The PC is not on Power saver, or it runs on battery.
ui.tweaks.why_not.PcieAspm: No capture pointed at a disk or network driver, and no stall came from a driver holding the processor.
ui.tweaks.why_not.UsbSuspend: No capture pointed at a USB driver.
ui.tweaks.why_not.SysMain: Windows is not on a hard disk, or the system disk was not busy for long.
ui.tweaks.why_not.WindowsSearch: Indexing never showed up as the cause of a busy disk or processor.
ui.tweaks.why_not.GameDvr: Background recording is off, or there were few stutters this week.
ui.tweaks.why_not.GpuScheduling: The video did not reset by itself and no report pointed at the video driver.
ui.tweaks.why_not.Mpo: This PC has one monitor, or there were no video resets or stutters.
ui.tweaks.why_not.StartupApp: It did not slow startup in the last full scan.
ui.tweaks.why_not.AppDumps: No app closed by itself in 30 days.
ui.tweaks.why_not.CrashDump: Windows already writes a dump on a blue screen.

ui.health.kind.MemoryTestErrors.title: The memory failed a test
ui.health.kind.MemoryTestErrors.tech: Windows Memory Diagnostic and the quick test
ui.health.kind.MemoryTestErrors.why: A memory test read back something different from what it wrote. That makes programs fail, files get damaged and the PC fall without a clear reason.
ui.health.kind.MemoryTestErrors.rule: Critical with MemoryDiagnostics-Results 1102 or 1202, or a quick test with errors in 90 days, until a clean Windows diagnostic comes after them.
ui.health.kind.DiskUnreadable.why.Critic: The whole-disk read found sectors the disk could not read. What was there may already be lost, and the damage tends to spread.
ui.health.kind.DiskUnreadable.why.Attent: On a hard disk, blocks that take more than half a second, twice in a row, are areas the disk struggles with.
ui.health.kind.DiskUnreadable.rule: Critical with any unreadable sector in the last surface scan; attention with 10 or more HDD blocks of 500 ms or more, read twice. A later clean scan closes it.
ui.health.kind.VolumeErrors.title: The file system of {subject} has problems
ui.health.kind.VolumeErrors.why: Windows found inconsistencies in how the files are organised on this volume. It repairs them itself at a restart; until then, a damaged file can fail to open.
ui.health.kind.VolumeErrors.rule: Attention when the last chkdsk /scan of the volume found problems; a later clean check closes it.
ui.occurrence.step.RunMemoryDiagnostic: Run the Windows memory test, in Tests; it runs at the next restart.
ui.occurrence.step.RunMemTest86: Confirm with MemTest86, from a USB stick, to find which memory module fails.
ui.occurrence.step.RepairVolume: Let Windows repair the volume: open its Properties › Tools › Check, and restart when it asks.
